Change: (1) Requirements tree: add a requirement (new id, e.g. R-STATES) in the design-core and/or the visual role requirements stating, with the reason, that every interactive element (buttons, links, inputs, toggles, list rows, menu items, tabs, cards that act) gets: a hover state where a pointer can hover; a pressed/active state on click or tap; a visible keyboard focus state (focus-visible on web); a disabled state where the control can be unavailable; mapped per platform: web and desktop need hover and pressed (and hover must not be the only way to reveal something, since touch and keyboard have no hover); iOS and Android have no hover, so pressed feedback (highlight, ripple, scale or opacity, per platform convention) carries it, plus focus for hardware keyboards; terminal UIs mark focus and selection instead; and that Worker.visual drives and captures each state (hover, pressed, focus, disabled) for each kind of interactive element before reporting, and Reviewer.visual exercises them and treats a missing state as material (interaction correctness).
